detailed_rationale:
Power Mech Projects is an engineering and construction contractor specializing in erection, testing and commissioning (ETC) of boilers, turbines and generators (BTG) for thermal power plants, along with balance-of-plant civil construction and operations & maintenance (O&M) services -- a business that benefits both from India's thermal-capacity revival (new coal-fired capacity being added to meet base-load demand growth alongside renewables) and from long-duration, annuity-like O&M contracts on the existing fleet.

FY26 revenue came in at ~Rs.6,062cr versus ~Rs.5,234cr in FY25 (~16% growth), with net profit up ~18% to ~Rs.412cr, continuing a strong 5-year trend (revenue CAGR ~26%, profit CAGR ~58%, though the latter clearly benefits from margin recovery off a smaller base in earlier years and should not be extrapolated). ROCE (~22%) and ROE (~16%) are healthy, borrowings declined modestly year-on-year (~Rs.735cr to ~Rs.664cr), and free cash flow -- negative in FY25 (~-Rs.159cr) on working-capital build -- turned positive in FY26 (~Rs.103cr), a constructive sign that the business is converting its growing order book into cash rather than just booked revenue. Promoter holding has drifted down modestly (~5.7 percentage points over three years), consistent with periodic equity raises to fund working capital in an EPC business rather than a governance flag by itself.
recommendation_rationale: Quant recommendation is Hold and our research supports it -- genuine, sector-tailwind-backed growth with improving cash conversion and no red flags -- but the business remains a cyclical EPC contractor dependent on India's thermal capex cycle continuing, which argues against treating it as an automatic rescue candidate; nothing here rises to escalation either.
summary: Power Mech Projects is a specialist contractor for thermal power plant construction and maintenance, benefiting from India's ongoing coal-capacity revival alongside its renewable buildout. Revenue and profit have both grown at a healthy mid-to-high-teens pace, debt has come down, and cash flow turned positive again after a working-capital-driven dip. We rate it a Hold: the sector tailwind and execution are both genuine, but this remains a cyclical, order-book-dependent EPC business rather than a structural compounder.
positive_para: Power Mech is well positioned for India's thermal-capacity revival cycle, with both new-build BTG erection work and recurring O&M contracts on the existing thermal fleet providing revenue visibility beyond just new order wins. Revenue and profit have both grown at a healthy mid-teens-plus pace with improving ROCE, and free cash flow turned positive again in FY26 after a working-capital-driven dip in FY25, showing the business can convert growth into cash rather than just booked revenue.
negative_para: This is fundamentally a cyclical EPC contractor whose growth depends on the pace of India's thermal (and broader power-sector) capex cycle continuing -- a slowdown in new thermal ordering, execution delays, or working-capital stress recurring (as it did in FY25) would directly hit growth and cash generation. The historical 5-year profit CAGR (~58%) partly reflects margin recovery off a smaller, weaker base and should not be read as a sustainable forward run-rate.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At a PE in the low-to-mid 20s against mid-to-high-teens delivered growth and healthy ROCE, the stock looks close to fairly valued for a well-executing thermal-power EPC contractor -- not clearly cheap, but not pricing in unrealistic hypergrowth either, provided the current India thermal-capex cycle continues at a similar pace.
